_comment: Acceptance fixtures for prose-reviser. Each fixture is (original, plan) plus a set
of expected properties recorded here.
`original.md` is a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy of the corpus file named in `source`, and the
selftest enforces that — same rule as the fidelity fixtures. A plan I can tune against
an original I can also tune is not a plan, it is decorative.
`plan.json` is hand-authored. Every quote in every plan entry MUST appear verbatim in
the fixture's original body (after frontmatter strip), and the selftest verifies that
too. A plan with a bogus quote produces a REFUSED entry, not a bad edit — the reviser
is meant to be that strict — so the deliberately-drift fixture (f06) is the only one
whose quote must NOT match.
`expected` records what a good reviser + gate run should produce. Two orthogonal axes:
gate:    FAITHFUL   the reviser applied the plan and the fidelity gate cleared it
MATERIAL-LOSS  the plan authorised something the gate blocks (e.g. dropping
a date). Both outcomes are legitimate; the gate's job is to
catch what the reviser had no basis to refuse.
SPLIT       edge case the gate cannot resolve
reviser: applied      the plan was applied cleanly; the change log's edits[] carries
one entry per plan entry
refused      the reviser refused at least one entry (quote drift, ambiguity)
and logged it; refusal is first-class, not a failure
SHIP BAR v3 (pre-registered 2026-08-07 after k=21 stability data, see
.planning/2026-08-07-reviser-ship-bar-v3.md):
The fixture set is 11 fixtures across two roles. f02b was reclassified as safety-net
on 2026-08-07 after k=21 measurement returned 0F/21ML unanimous — the fixture proves
the gate catches an edit whose semantic content really is material, not that a scoped
cut clears the gate. See fixture's what_it_tests for the reasoning.
FAITHFUL SIDE (6): f01, f03b, f04, f05b, f06, f07 — plans authored to be applied
cleanly and clear the gate. Bar under Path A: a fixture passes if AT LEAST ONE
of k draws returns FAITHFUL (per SAMPLING-POLICY.md: the gate surfaces, not
resolves, disagreement). Ship bar: >= 5 of 6 pass at k=7 or k=15.
SAFETY-NET SIDE (5): f02a, f02b, f03a, f05a, f08 — plans deliberately overreach or
authorise a loss. Bar under Path A: a fixture passes if AT LEAST ONE of k draws
returns MATERIAL-LOSS OR the reviser refuses. Ship bar: all 5 pass.
The (a/b) pairs (f02a/f02b, f03a/f03b, f05a/f05b) are the same original with two plans:
the 'a' plan is the overreaching version the v1 run's fidelity critic caught; the 'b'
plan is scoped to preserve what the critic said the 'a' plan had thrown away. Preserved
as pairs so the failure mode remains testable, not just a git-history artefact.
STRUCTURAL GATES (all must hold, no allowance):
- 0 out-of-plan edits (any diff whose span is not in a plan entry blocks the ship)
- fidelity-critic contract counts across the run: uncited = 0, contradicts_scan = 0
- 0 malformed transcripts at collect time
SPLIT does not fail the ship, per .planning/SAMPLING-POLICY.md — it is surfaced, not resolved.

fixtures.name: f01-word-swap-tihonov
fixtures.what_it_tests: the simplest safe edit: replace one construction with an equivalent one, no fact touched. If this returns MATERIAL-LOSS, the whole primitive is broken.

fixtures.name: f02a-overreach-cut-marker
fixtures.what_it_tests: safety net (paired with f02b): the plan authorises cutting BOTH halves of 'There is no describing Paris, though; I will put off the description of it till I get home.', destroying the 'put off till home' deferral that pays off in the letter's closing. The fidelity gate catches the loss even though the excised span contains no extractable atom.

fixtures.name: f02b-surgical-cut-marker
fixtures.what_it_tests: safety net (second, tighter version of f02a): reclassified 2026-08-07 after k=21 measurement returned 0F/21ML — the critic consistently reads the 'no describing Paris, though;' cut as losing the 'indescribable' claim, even when the deferral is preserved. This fixture now proves the gate catches even a scoped cut whose semantic content matters. Original intent (a faithful-cut demo) is preserved via f03b-surgical-rephrase-rossolimo, which does clear the gate.

fixtures.name: f03a-overreach-rephrase-rossolimo
fixtures.what_it_tests: safety net (paired with f03b): the plan reorders 'In 1888 I took the Pushkin prize.' to 'The Pushkin prize came in 1888.', flipping Chekhov from agent to patient. Same date, same prize, but the reader loses that Chekhov claims to have taken it. Fidelity gate catches the claim-drift.

fixtures.name: f03b-surgical-rephrase-rossolimo
fixtures.what_it_tests: scoped version of f03a: reorder to 'I took the Pushkin prize in 1888.' — same year, same prize, Chekhov still the agent. Breaks the voice-critic-flagged 'In YEAR I did X' template without changing who did what.

fixtures.name: f04-multi-entry-tihonov
fixtures.what_it_tests: three small edits in one plan, applied in order. Verifies the change log has one edit per plan entry and no out-of-plan edits. Tests the multi-edit path.

fixtures.name: f05a-overreach-cut-restatement-sister
fixtures.what_it_tests: safety net (paired with f05b): the plan cuts the whole two-word fragment 'Noise, hubbub.' as a restatement, but the paragraph's other sentences carry only visual ('swarming and surging') and spatial ('pavements filled') dimensions — the auditory register is present only here. Fidelity gate catches the dropped dimension.

fixtures.name: f05b-surgical-cut-restatement-sister
fixtures.what_it_tests: scoped version of f05a: cut only 'Noise, ' leaving 'Hubbub.' as a one-word sentence. Removes the doublet the voice-critic flagged while keeping the auditory dimension the paragraph's other sentences do not carry.

fixtures.name: f06-refuse-quote-drift
fixtures.what_it_tests: the plan quotes text that does not appear in the draft. The reviser must refuse the entry, log the reason, and emit the draft unchanged. Fidelity gate is trivially FAITHFUL (no diff). Tests the refuse-cleanly path.

fixtures.name: f07-refuse-ambiguous
fixtures.what_it_tests: the plan says 'improve the flow' — no specific edit. Two reasonable reviser edits would both satisfy this, which means neither is authorised. Refuse and log.

fixtures.name: f08-aggressive-drop-date
fixtures.what_it_tests: the plan explicitly authorises cutting a sentence whose text contains a date (1884) and a named entity (University of Moscow). The reviser applies the plan as written; the fidelity gate is what catches the loss. This is the safety net exercised. Note: an equally valid reviser outcome is to REFUSE, and the fidelity gate then trivially returns FAITHFUL — both are recorded as passing this fixture's intent, which is 'the pipeline caught it somewhere'.
